$comment: Capability registry — the single source of truth for what each security/reliability capability of ApexMail ACTUALLY is, versus what the marketing/compliance surfaces say about it. Companion to docs/development/topology-manifest.json (which owns runtime topology; this file owns capability truth). tools/check_capability_claims.py proves: (a) every entry at stage >= runtime-wired has evidence that EXISTS in the tree — docker_target present in BOTH the Dockerfile (FROM runtime-base AS <target>) and topology-manifest.json, compose_service present in the compose files, and evidence.env_gate.name greppable in the wiring crate's Rust sources (null env_gate = always-on wiring, allowed); (b) the claim surfaces (marketing security/architecture pages + compliance templates) may NAME a sub-runtime-wired capability (stage < runtime-wired) only inside explicit [roadmap]-marked context — every scan_aliases hit outside that context on a surface is a claim that the capability must be at stage >= runtime-wired or the gate FAILS (advertised == deployed, both directions driven by the per-capability alias lists below); (c) crate README wiring-status lines match registry stages: stage >= runtime-wired forbids a 'NOT WIRED INTO PRODUCTION' banner (unless a stale_marker_exceptions needle still proves the banner stale) and requires the env-gate name to appear in the README when one is declared; stage < runtime-wired requires the banner or an explicit 'wiring in flight' statement. Strictness: CAPABILITY_GATE_STRICT=0 (default) prints in-flight wiring items as WARN and exits 0; =1 fails on them. Set it to 1 once the in_flight_wiring items below have landed.

stage_rules.implemented: code exists; nothing consumes it outside its own crate
stage_rules.integration-tested: consumed by crates/{integration-tests,fuzz-tests,perf-tests,load-tests} only — zero production call path
stage_rules.runtime-wired: a production binary constructs/mounts it in a live request or delivery path (monitor/flag-gated counts — say so in evidence)
stage_rules.deployed: runtime-wired AND running in the prod compose topology with default-on behavior
stage_rules.monitored: deployed AND covered by an alerting rule / dashboard in deploy/
stage_rules.advertised: deployed+monitored truthfully AND the marketing claim matches the wired behavior — only this stage may be named in claim surfaces outside [roadmap] context

scan.context_rule: A capability alias may appear on a claim surface only (1) on a line that itself contains the marker, or (2) anywhere between a marker line and the next markdown heading (line starting with '#') or the marker_close line. Markdown ATX headings are not scanned (they organize; they do not claim). Everything else is a bare capability-name drop: it requires the named capability at stage >= runtime-wired and FAILS the gate otherwise. Limitation (by design): the gate can only police the capability names enumerated in scan_aliases below — a NEW product claim about a capability that has no alias entry is invisible to it, so every new security/reliability claim must add its alias here in the same change.
scan.word_boundary_tokens: aliases shorter than 5 chars or all-caps acronyms are matched with word boundaries (\b) so 'SSO' does not hit inside longer words; phrase aliases are matched as case-insensitive substrings.

in_flight_wiring.$comment: Wiring contracts agreed with the crate owners but whose code has not landed in the tree yet. The checker prints these as WARN lines (CAPABILITY_GATE_STRICT=1 turns an UNLANDED entry below whose registry stage was already raised into a failure; while the stage honestly stays below runtime-wired these are informational). Each entry names the env gate that WILL gate it so the registry/gate/READMEs agree on the contract before the code arrives.

stale_marker_exceptions.$comment: crates/*/README.md markers that are STALE relative to the dep graph (the crate IS consumed by a production binary). Each exception carries <file>:<needle> pairs that the checker greps — if the wiring disappears (or the crate owner fixes the README marker), the exception goes stale and the checker FAILS, forcing this registry to be re-triaged. Crates are owned by the mail-server agents; this registry may not edit their READMEs.
stale_marker_exceptions.waf-engine: Marker says 'no service in this workspace (api-server, mta, worker, …) depends on this crate' — stale since the F-WIRING-1 remediation wired it into api-server (monitor mode).
